caption: School taught you what success looks like. It never asked what it feels like.

slides.text:
How School Conditioned Your Definition of Success

(The Unlearning Method)

1. Notice the grading

“We don't grow into creativity, we grow out of it. Or rather, we get educated out of it.” – Sir Ken Robinson

For 12+ years, success meant
• the right answer
• a good grade
• approval from someone above you

So you still wait for someone to tell you you're doing GOOD.

No one talks about this -

School rewarded you for
• sitting still
• following instructions
• avoiding mistakes

Building a life you love asks for the opposite.

The ones who create something real had to UNLEARN being a good student.

2. Find your old report card

Ask yourself:
• Whose approval am I still working for?
• What would “success” mean if nobody graded it?
• What did I love before someone called it impractical?

Write your answers down. Today.

3. The final framework

How to unlearn it:

1. STOP waiting for permission

2. MAKE mistakes on purpose. They're data, not failure

3. MEASURE success by how free you feel

4. FOLLOW what you'd do with no audience

4. Grade yourself

Remember - the system needed you to fit in.

Your purpose needs you to STAND OUT.

You're not behind. You're finally writing your own definition.

This is the Key.

Save this for the next time you feel “behind.”
